trigger: decomposition as drafted keyed the <=2-active-rotation invariant on the principal, which is true for an engine principal (one credential) and false for a human (N tokens)
classification_rationale: the plan asserted an invariant the human arm does not satisfy
summary: Plan gate BLOCK before any code: P1 re-scoped to token-keyed arbitration, <=2 active per rotation_group rather than per principal.

trigger: Gate 1 Resource Ledger enumerated production boundaries only and omitted six test-side ones (3x PGconn*, 2x thread, 1x Lease)
classification_rationale: a required Gate 1 artefact was incomplete; it contradicts nothing, it is missing
summary: Senior-authored Resource Ledger short by six boundaries. Gates as a contract violation, not by derivation - it has no wrong outcome in production.

trigger: senior approved granting ApiToken:Write to the operator role so self-service rotation would be reachable
classification_rationale: securable-wide Write is enforced cross-transport by AuthRoutes::require_permission, so the grant also widened create and delete
summary: Privilege escalation approved by the senior and caught at the gate: ApiToken:Write @ operator widened far past rotation. Replaced with a dedicated ApiToken:Rotate operation.

trigger: the ApiToken:Rotate remedy let a caller nominate any predecessor they own; the successor inherited the predecessor mcp_tier and scope_service verbatim
classification_rationale: the first remedy for SEC-1 reintroduced escalation by a different route
adjudicated_by: enterprise-architect (fable), not the change author - de-escalation rule separation
adjudication_rationale: equality on the (mcp_tier, scope_service) pair was chosen over a tier lattice: a lattice is a new authority ordering to get wrong, equality is checkable. The de-escalating direction is deliberately also blocked; the cost is recorded as issue #2963.
summary: Tier escalation via caller-chosen predecessor. Fixed by requiring predecessor.(mcp_tier, scope_service) == caller.(mcp_tier, scope_service).

trigger: caller_mcp_tier and caller_scope_service were declared with = "" defaults, so a call site that forgot them matched the untiered predecessor
classification_rationale: cpp-safety read the same default as strictest and security-guardian as most permissive; security-guardian was upheld by the senior - "" is the untiered value and therefore the exploit target, not a safe floor
summary: Default-argument authority parameters silently defeated the SEC-2 guard. Defaults removed and the required parameters positioned before the optional one, so a copied 4-arg call fails to compile.

trigger: store_rotation_raw was hoisted above the if (!ok) COMMIT check to satisfy a senior instruction to scrub on every exit path; a COMMIT failure then left an unevictable grace-cache entry
classification_rationale: the cache entry keyed a row that was never committed, so nothing could ever evict it
summary: Senior instruction named an outcome (scrub on every exit) without naming a mechanism, and the builder chose reordering. Fixed by restoring the engine ordering and using ScopeExit for the scrub.

trigger: a new rotation error string collided with an existing substring key in engine_store_error_class.hpp, so a 400-class condition classified as 409
classification_rationale: substring-keyed classification is order-dependent and the new key was shadowed
summary: Found only by tests written blind against the contract, not by any reviewer reading the diff.

trigger: a server restart inside the overlap window destroys the process-local grace cache, so confirmed_at is never written and the sweep cuts over on the timer with no error surfaced
classification_rationale: the feature advertises operator-confirmed cutover as a control that a routine restart disables; I6 raises to HIGH under the FALSE ASSURANCE clause
summary: Durable rotation state paired with a non-durable, non-shared consent record. Present on the engine arm too. Deferred by operator decision to re-cut the durability cluster separately.

trigger: confirm has no time bound, and a failed resolve_rotation_pair_after_revoke leaves the surviving token in a state no operation can advance
classification_rationale: wedged state machine - I5 raises to HIGH under clause (c)
summary: Rotation can reach unrecoverable terminals. Both arms.

trigger: the sweep revokes the predecessor at overlap expiry even when the successor last_used_at == 0, i.e. the successor was never demonstrably received
classification_rationale: the sweep is the sole cutover enforcer and has no successor-received precondition
summary: Lockout on a rotation the holder never completed. Being fixed in this run (Gate 7 round 3).

trigger: sweep_expired_rotations selects on overlap_expires_at <= now - a bare wall-clock cutoff with no persisted anchor, no sanitisation, no anomaly suppression and no per-tick cap; a forward NTP step cuts over every in-flight rotation fleet-wide in one tick
classification_rationale: the routed concern mandates the seven-part guarded shape for any bulk wall-clock-driven mutation; none of it is present
summary: Split by operator decision: the unconditional per-tick cap (the half that always applies) is being added in this run; the detector suite is deferred to #2964 with the missing-anchor decision explicitly left to be made and recorded rather than copied.

trigger: RBAC ships OFF, so the legacy fallback makes every non-Read op admin-only; composed with the store self-service-only rule, only an admin can rotate and only their own tokens. Separately the SEC-2 authority guard makes a tiered token unrotatable from an untiered interactive session
classification_rationale: the capability the change presents is not reachable in the default configuration by the population it exists for; security-guardian independently flagged the de-escalating-direction half at Gate 8
summary: Reachability is a product question, not a patch: filed as a decision issue rather than resolved unilaterally at the gate.

trigger: a committed successor mint is audited as a failure when a later non-transactional step errors
classification_rationale: the audit record contradicts the committed database state
summary: Audit ordering: the record must not report a committed mint as a failure. Being fixed in this run (Gate 7 round 3).

trigger: no rotate-side metric exists at all; docs/prometheus/yuzu-alerts.yml was not touched, so the four pre-seeded human rotation families and yuzu_api_token_confirm_total have no rule referencing them
classification_rationale: a required observability surface for a shipped behaviour change is missing
summary: No rotation failure mode is alertable.

trigger: the senior unblocked the docs piece against the pre-P4 base to parallelise it and never re-ran it after P4 merged
classification_rationale: five doc statements described a surface that P4 had changed; the docs were not wrong when written, they were never re-read against the merged tree
summary: Temporal seam introduced by the senior, not by any builder. The skill was amended mid-run: quiesce a piece before reviewing it, and stay quiesced until every reviewer is back.

trigger: the senior asserted "three specialists reviewed this" in a compliance record from recollection; a reviewer declined to corroborate it - c1325015 records two, and no governance.d fragment existed
classification_rationale: an independence claim routed through the reviewed party is not evidence of independent review - the exact property the source/reporter_ref split exists to protect
summary: Claim withdrawn and this ledger fragment created so the reviewer count is a record rather than a recollection.

trigger: confirm_rotation / confirm_token_rotation fall through past the kPair branch and return a retryable 503 for a state that is terminal
classification_rationale: a terminal condition answered as retryable makes the caller loop forever
summary: Pre-existing on the engine arm, generalised into the human arm by construction. Both arms affected. Not introduced by this change; filed rather than fixed here.

trigger: the engine rotate response reads overlap_expires_at off the successor row, where it is a structural 0, and stamps it on the predecessor
classification_rationale: the wire contract reports a field the caller needs, with a value that is always zero
summary: Found by holding the human arm to the engine arm as its bar - the bar itself was wrong here. Pre-existing engine defect, filed at operator instruction.

trigger: a supervised-tier token can mint itself a token carrying no tier, which is then perpetual and unrestricted
classification_rationale: tier confinement is escapable by the confined principal itself
summary: Pre-existing token-minting escalation surfaced while deriving the rotation authority guard. Filed with the security label; out of scope for this change and not fixed here.

trigger: the sweep revokes the predecessor at overlap expiry even when the successor last_used_at == 0
classification_rationale: resolved in Gate 7 round 3
summary: sweep_expired_rotations now declines to auto-revoke while the successor is unpresented, re-checked under the locked transaction rather than the earlier unlocked scan. Dedicated test verified to fail against the pre-fix code (4 assertion failures).

trigger: bare wall-clock sweep cutoff with no cap and no detectors
classification_rationale: the cap half is now present; the detector half is not
adjudicated_by: operator (Fraser Jarvis), not a subagent of the authoring session
adjudication_rationale: the routed concern itself states the cap is the half that ALWAYS applies and the detectors are best-effort, so shipping the cap and re-cutting the detectors is a split along the concern own seam, not a waiver. The missing-anchor decision is deliberately left unmade rather than copied from a sibling store - the concern is explicit that the recorded reasoning is what makes any of these correct.
summary: kMaxAutoRevokesPerTick=200 landed with yuzu_engine_principal_rotation_sweep_capped_total. Detector suite and the missing-anchor decision carried to #2964. Note the value is untested against real fleet concurrency - flagged by the implementer, not independently validated.

trigger: a committed successor mint audited as a failure when the read-back errors
classification_rationale: resolved in Gate 7 round 3
summary: Both transports now audit "partial" - an established result value in this codebase (sle_routes.cpp, server.cpp), stored verbatim and fully queryable; it buckets to the Prometheus other series, which is pre-existing behaviour for every partial call site. Caller-facing 503 unchanged. MCP test verified to fail pre-fix.

reporter: senior (Gate 8 verification of the round-3 fix)
trigger: UP-5 leaves a never-used pair open indefinitely; the round-3 fix then bypassed the warning de-dup once elapsed, so the audit row was written on every 60s sweep tick, per stuck pair, forever
classification_rationale: unbounded growth on the audit store - I5 raises to HIGH under clause (b), a serialised path shared with a data-integrity operation; I2 because the audit retention pass caps at 25000 deletions, so ~1440 rows/day/pair displaces genuine SOC 2 evidence
summary: Extracted the cadence decision into rotation_warn_dedup.hpp so it is testable at all - it previously lived inline in a ServerImpl thread lambda, which is exactly why it reached review unexamined. Log repeats per tick; counter and audit are once per pair per state, preserving the pre-existing counter semantics rather than silently converting the series into a rate. Six-case test verified to fail against pre-fix semantics (5/6 cases fail).

trigger: an operator whose token is within 24h of its own expiry calls rotate; any legal overlap_secs (24h floor) would outlive the predecessor, so the store returns a bare 400 and the error-matrix row gives no remediation
classification_rationale: the mechanical constraint is fully disclosed elsewhere; what is missing is inline guidance at the error row. Not a concealed breaking change, so I7 stays at base and does not raise.
summary: The end-of-life rotation dead zone is documented as a constraint but not as a symptom. Folded into the existing decision issue rather than filed separately - #2963 already asks what the intended path is for a token nearing expiry, and the doc wording follows from whatever is decided.

trigger: comparing the REST rotate response (raw secret under `token`) with the MCP rotate_api_token response (identical value under `raw_token`)
classification_rationale: a real cross-transport naming divergence, but the reporter's implied remedy (rename the new route) is wrong: POST /api/v1/tokens already returns `token`, so the rotate route matched its own REST sibling correctly. The divergence is surface-wide (REST human tokens use `token`; MCP and the REST engine-credential surface use `raw_token`) and predates this change.
summary: Recorded against the existing open parity issue, whose scope was widened by comment to cover the human arm so a future reconcile does not land engine-only. Not changed here: renaming in isolation would trade a cross-transport inconsistency for a within-transport one.

trigger: any sweep tick that fails, or hits kMaxAutoRevokesPerTick, while human-owned rotation pairs are in flight
classification_rationale: rotation_sweep_naming.hpp:20-27 states the rule this whole change establishes - a human row must never be reported under an engine_principal-named series. The two TICK-level counters keep the engine name and amend only their HELP text. The non-attribution argument justifies not SPLITTING, not keeping the engine NAME; a kind-neutral name satisfies both.
summary: Splits in two and only half is free: yuzu_engine_principal_rotation_sweep_capped_total is NEW in this change and never shipped, so renaming it kind-neutral costs nothing; ..._sweep_failures_total is pre-existing and renaming it breaks any existing alert. Held for the sre gate, which owns metric naming and is still running - deciding this myself would repeat the error I already flagged once this run.

trigger: a human principal_id owning any active row with principal_kind='engine'
classification_rationale: the last surviving engine-arm premise in the human arm: both new arms abort on a PRINCIPAL-WIDE property while everything else is correctly group-scoped. E6 because engine credentials are only minted against `engine:`-prefixed principal ids and principal_id here is the authenticated human username, so the wrong outcome cannot occur today.
summary: Code is right, recorded reason is the engine arm's. The UP-5 guard comments (api_token_store.cpp:1951, :2040, :2053) justify a group-scoped guard with 'dropping the principal to ZERO credentials', which is false for a human holding other tokens - the true statement is zero usable credentials for this ROTATION GROUP. That matters because the reason is what gets weighed if anyone is later asked to relax UP-5 for humans.

trigger: a rotate or confirm by a human principal holding a large number of active API tokens
classification_rationale: read_active_for_principal_on_conn has no LIMIT and runs inside the advisory-locked write transaction. The set size was bounded at <=2 by construction in the engine arm and is unbounded here - nothing caps how many tokens a human may hold (principal_quota* is engine-only). Blast radius is self-limited: the advisory lock is per-principal and statement_timeout bounds the query.
summary: Not a request to make the SQL group-scoped - the in-memory filter is the right design and rotation_confirm_state.hpp's rationale for it is correct. The narrow point is that a cost premise silently changed when the arm went token-keyed, and nothing records that.

trigger: none at runtime - the recorded justification for leaving a copyable RAII guard is false as reasoning
classification_rationale: the comment says deleting copy/move would break every call site because 'no converting constructor exists to take its place' - true as written but reads as none COULD exist, which the reviewer disproved by compiling `explicit ScopeExit(F f)` with deleted copy/move against the existing CTAD call sites. NOT a policy floor: ScopeExit is a local RAII helper, not a chokepoint named by a routed-concern row, a CLAUDE.md invariant block, or an ADR.
summary: The DUPLICATION is defensible and the reviewer explicitly declined to ask for a shared header - that would create a server<->agent dependency edge that does not exist. What fails is the stated reason. Ownership call on a copyable RAII guard belongs to cpp-safety.

trigger: describe() is called for yuzu_engine_principal_rotation_sweep_capped_total with no companion counter() call at startup, so the family is ABSENT from /metrics - not present-at-zero - until the first capped tick
classification_rationale: observability-conventions promises bounded-label counters are pre-seeded to 0 so absent()-style alerts stay meaningful; that guarantee does not hold here. Reproduced by standalone compile against sdk/include/yuzu/metrics.hpp - describe() only populates descriptions_, serialize() emits nothing until counter() is called once.
summary: Worst on the one series that matters most: increase()>0 needs two in-range samples, so an alert can structurally MISS the first (possibly only) capped tick - the tick that signals a clock jump. One-line fix. The pre-existing ..._failures_total has the identical gap; same fix, no rename involved, so no compatibility cost.

trigger: a pool-lease timeout or failed SELECT inside list_rotations_nearing_expiry_unused - it logs a warning and returns an empty vector, with no bool* out-param and no throw
classification_rationale: exactly the silent-degradation class sweep_failures_total was created to eliminate, recurring on the OTHER half of the same sweep. The caller cannot distinguish 'nothing nearing expiry' from 'the scan failed', and the enclosing try/catch cannot catch what is never thrown.
summary: Second-order consequence found by the same reviewer: an empty result from a FAILED scan feeds warn_dedup.prune({}), wiping every tracked pair's de-dup state, so previously-audited stuck pairs re-fire their audit row once the fault clears. That partially re-opens the flood this run just fixed.

trigger: an on-call engineer paged off the successor_unused signal has no consolidated recipe - rotate/confirm/revoke are documented only in isolation
classification_rationale: the reporter was explicit that this is its own domain judgement and NOT the governance policy-floor 'required documentation' list - no routed-concern row names an ops-runbook as an update obligation for this surface. Recorded at native severity accordingly.
summary: Precedent is established: audit-store-clock-guard.md, engine-principal-store-recovery.md and mcp-bridge-teardown-recovery.md all shipped alongside their operational-health signals. The log line tells the operator the pair stays active until they act, but not which primitive is safe in which sub-case (successor genuinely lost vs merely not yet installed).

trigger: senior asked the metrics owner to adjudicate holding the successor_unused counter to once-per-state rather than per-tick
classification_rationale: the cadence is RATIFIED - a counter has one honest meaning and per-tick would make one series an event count for pre-elapse pairs and a disguised rate for elapsed ones. But the conclusion drawn from it (accept that there is no alertable signal) is REJECTED: the right instrument is a gauge, not a rate.
adjudicated_by: sre governance agent, not the change author
adjudication_rationale: RotationWarnDedup::tracked_elapsed() already computes the live count of currently-stuck past-window pairs and is one comment away from being publishable. A gauge re-set each tick is definitionally a current-state reading, carries none of the semantic-mixing risk, needs no de-dup, and costs nothing against the audit retention budget that drove the cadence decision in the first place.
summary: Do not touch the counter. Publish tracked_elapsed() as a gauge instead - the deliberate new signal the header comment already anticipates needing. Recommended into #2964 rather than a new issue.

trigger: an auditor follows the pointer at docs/auth-architecture.md:2022-2024, which names five audit verbs as documented in docs/user-manual/audit-log.md; only api_token.rotation.auto_revoke and .successor_unused are there (plus pre-existing .create/.revoke). api_token.rotate, .confirm and .reveal have no verb-table row.
classification_rationale: I7 raises to HIGH: the omission conceals security-relevant behaviour in the routed-concern-designated audit reference, and the missing verbs are the INITIATOR-side events for a CC6.3-labelled control. E3 because a document is read by an operator, never reached by an attacker, so it caps at HIGH.
summary: Verified independently by the senior before acceptance: the claim in auth-architecture.md and the contents of audit-log.md were read side by side. The three initiator-side verbs the REST/MCP surface actually emits on every rotate/reveal/confirm are absent from the canonical reference that this feature's own design doc says contains them.

trigger: docs/security-reviews/human-token-rotation-2026-08-10.md declares its purpose as recording the evidence chain; its Open risks section lists only #2943/#2944/#2945. #2961 (P1, security), #2962 (P1), #2963 (P1, decision) and #2964 (P2) were filed the same day off this same range and appear nowhere in the document.
classification_rationale: I7 raises to HIGH: the omission conceals a security-relevant limitation - #2961 is the durability of the maker-checker confirm control itself - from the one document whose stated function is to be the compliance evidence record.
summary: Verified: grep for #29xx across the whole document returns only 2943, 2944, 2945. The deferrals were deliberate and adjudicated, and the ledger proves that; the shipped evidence doc does not carry it.

trigger: governance.d/local-human-token-rotation.rToPDo.jsonl is untracked while three commits on the branch already fix findings it records; git ls-files shows every other fragment in repo history is committed
classification_rationale: governance.d/README.md is explicit that the fragment is committed precisely because CC8.1 evidence must be retrievable by someone other than the person who generated it (#2618). Untracked, it is not yet evidence.
summary: The reviewer notes this is the precondition for CO-F2's fix to mean anything - the record showing the #2961-class deferrals were reviewed decisions rather than oversights does not exist in the repo. Also flags the local- prefix should become the PR number once one exists.

trigger: api_token.reveal audits target_id = the PREDECESSOR's id with detail 'rotate'; api_token.confirm audits target_id = the SUCCESSOR's id with detail 'confirmed'. Neither names the other side of the pair, and neither carries rotation_group.
classification_rationale: the engine arm does not have this problem because it audits by principal_id throughout, which is a stable join key when a principal holds one credential. The human arm deliberately cannot use principal_id as a join key - one principal may have several concurrent rotations - and nothing was substituted. The sweep's own .successor_unused row already embeds predecessor_token_id for exactly this reason.
summary: Each row is individually accurate; what is missing is a shared correlation key, so reconstructing one rotation's reveal-to-confirm lifecycle needs timestamp/principal inference. Another instance of the engine premise surviving into the token-keyed arm - same class as architect's A-2.

trigger: the Rotating a Token walkthrough presents confirm and the auto-revoke sweep as two equally good paths to the same end state, with no caveat that a restart inside the default 7-day window permanently forecloses confirm for that pair
classification_rationale: the 409 symptom IS documented in the REST error table, so this is lighter than F1/F2's outright false claims - the gap is that the walkthrough an operator actually reads before relying on confirm does not cross-reference it.
summary: Kept at MEDIUM natively by the reporter rather than raised, on the stated grounds that the underlying symptom is documented elsewhere in the same change.

trigger: docs/user-manual/audit-log.md:163 states the successor_unused audit row 'fires every tick once the window has elapsed and the successor is still unused' - true at f61d65b7, made FALSE by commit c25b6f79, which bounded the audit row to once per pair per state
classification_rationale: the audit-log reference describes when the AUDIT ROW fires; after c25b6f79 only the LOG LINE fires per tick. I7 raises to HIGH - it misdescribes the cadence of a compliance-evidence row in the canonical audit reference, so an auditor sizing evidence volume, or an operator diagnosing a missing row, is misled.
summary: Found by the senior while verifying CO-F1, NOT reported by any gate - compliance-officer read this file at c25b6f79 and did not catch it. Self-inflicted: my own fix changed the behaviour and I did not sweep the docs for statements about the old cadence. Same class as the temporal-seam error earlier in this run.

trigger: an operator rotates, never presents the successor (dropped response, lost secret), and follows the walkthrough's advice to skip confirm. The sweep's predecessor scan requires the successor's last_used_at <> 0, so the predecessor is NEVER auto-revoked and both credentials stay live indefinitely.
classification_rationale: the doc states a shipped behaviour incorrectly and the omission conceals a security-relevant one - a credential the operator is told will auto-revoke does not. I4 was considered and rejected by the reporter because the wedged state is visible in GET /api/v1/tokens, so it fails diagnosably.
summary: The sharpest instance: docs/user-manual/engine-principals.md was corrected FOR THE ENGINE ARM IN THIS SAME COMMIT with the right wording ('unless the successor was never presented at all, in which case the sweep deliberately leaves BOTH credentials active'), while the new human walkthrough shipped the uncorrected sentence. One sweep, one carve-out, two operator docs in one change, one right and one wrong. Explicitly NOT covered by #2962, which defers the wedged-survivor behaviour, not a doc asserting the opposite of shipped behaviour.

trigger: a rotation pair whose window has elapsed with an unused successor: three doc sites claim the successor_unused audit row fires every sweep tick; RotationWarnDedup fires it once per pair per state, and server.cpp's `if (!signals.record_event) continue;` gates both the metric increment and the audit row
classification_rationale: conceals a security-relevant behaviour: audit-log.md:161 asserts a DETECTION property ('so a stuck-open rotation cannot go silent') that is false, and rotation_warn_dedup.hpp's own header says the opposite in as many words.
summary: Subsumes SG8-DOCSTALE, which the senior found independently while verifying CO-F1 but scoped to audit-log.md:163 only. This reporter found three sites: audit-log.md:161, :163 and engine-principals.md:112-115 - the last of which then advises the operator to act 'once that warning is firing past the window's own end', on a signal that fires once. independent_reporters=2.

trigger: an authenticated owner calls confirm from a session whose mcp_tier/scope_service differ from the token's; the store returns 'no such token to confirm', the classifier maps it to ClientValidation, and the route answers 400 - a status the embedded OpenAPI says it cannot produce
classification_rationale: the machine-readable contract served via /api/v1/discover/routes and MCP discover_routes disagrees with the published rest-api.md, which carries the full 400 matrix. Not raised to HIGH: rest-api.md states the truth, so nothing security-relevant is concealed.
summary: confirm declares no 400 at all; rotate enumerates three causes where at least eight reach it. Note the reporter cleared the CLASSIFIER itself: it walked all 66 new error strings through the seven ordered steps and found no new collision on either transport.

trigger: tools/call rotate_api_token with overlap_days as a JSON float (30.0) or string ("30") - what a Python or JS client emits for a float. param_int tests is_number_integer() and silently returns the 7-day default; the 1..3650 range check then passes.
classification_rationale: the REST twin explicitly 400s on the same shape, a strictness fix the code comment attributes to round-3 review - applied on one transport only. Not I3: the response's overlap_expires_at reports the effective window, so the caller can tell.
summary: The declared "type":"integer" bound is not enforced at the handler (A5 secondary). The pre-existing engine twin at :8840 has it too - fix both, or fix param_int's contract.

trigger: reading .claude/skills/auth-and-authz/SKILL.md after this commit: line 143 states that grepping mcp_server.cpp for rotate_token/confirm_token_rotation 'returns no hits, confirming the MCP twins genuinely have no merged code' - false as of this commit (mcp_server.cpp:9107, :9316) - and it sits immediately above the item-11 rewrite saying the twins ARE shipped
classification_rationale: a routed-concern row names this file as the A&A roadmap doc and the standing instruction is not to re-plan shipped work; a planner reading the stale verification stamp re-scopes work that exists.
summary: Self-contradiction inside one commit. Secondary on the same row: line 49 still says 22 securable types and omits EnginePrincipal, while authz_model.hpp was corrected to 23 in THIS diff and rbac_store.cpp seeds 23.

trigger: rename a name inside kEngineRotationSweepNames: the sweep driver picks it up because it reads names.*, but server.cpp:1979,1983 still describe() the engine names as string literals, producing an undescribed series
classification_rationale: exactly the drift rotation_sweep_naming.hpp's header claims the symbol export prevents - true only of the human half it was written for. Separately the human auto_revoked/events families ARE pre-seeded to 0 and their engine twins are not, so a symmetric alert pair across two families the docs call twins behaves asymmetrically.
summary: Converges with sre's SRE-F1 (pre-seeding) and architect's note on the engine describe literals - three reviewers reached the registration block independently from different directions.

trigger: relocating tests/unit/server/ or server/core/src/, or copying this test elsewhere - the ../../../ path breaks while the bare-form siblings keep working
classification_rationale: tests/meson.build:694 already puts ../server/core/src on this exe's include path, so the relative form is unnecessary; the ~20 other server tests use the bare form.
summary: Senior-authored. Forward slashes are fine on MSVC so this is brittleness, not a break.

trigger: a standard library that does not transitively expose std::size_t through <string>/<unordered_set> - not any shipping libstdc++, libc++ or MSVC STL, so no concrete trigger exists today
classification_rationale: IWYU hygiene, not a predicted break - the reporter was explicit about that and recorded `likely` rather than `verified` accordingly.
summary: Senior-authored, and the same omission the round-3 fix had just corrected in rotation_confirm_state.hpp - I created a new header and repeated it.

trigger: a future edit to the REST rotate handler's !successor.found branch reverting "partial" to "failure" - verified concretely by direct mutation plus a full [rotation]-suite rerun (128 cases, 2116 assertions, PG on): ZERO failures
classification_rationale: the reporter flagged that the taxonomy is built for production-code findings and does not map cleanly to a test-suite gap, per the preamble's own instruction to say so. NOT a policy floor: the existing MCP test is legitimate and observes what it asserts - this is an absent test on the twin arm, which the floor carve-out treats as SHOULD.
summary: The UP-11 fix is two independent hand-written copies of a compliance-relevant string literal, one arm tested. The reporter cites this repo's own precedent against the implementer's judgement: the dispatch-targeting routed-concern row says in as many words that 'a second copy is how the identical defect survived on REST after MCP was fixed'. Accepted - the implementer's one-test call is overturned.

trigger: n/a - evidence-accuracy note about the Change Summary, not a code defect
classification_rationale: the senior's gate brief asserted six amended pre-existing tests, relayed uncritically from the fix agent's own RISKS section. Exhaustive body-diff of all 54 pre-existing test cases at merge-base plus a git grep of every sweep_expired_rotations call site shows 3: two in test_api_token_store.cpp, one in test_engine_principal_lifecycle.cpp.
summary: No coverage was lost - the reporter fault-injected all three and each still fails on a regression in its own named subject. The defect is that I passed a subagent's self-reported number to eight reviewers as fact. Recorded so a future reader does not skip re-deriving it.

trigger: copying build-linux wholesale into a scratch worktree: ninja's self-regeneration re-runs meson from cached coredata and rewrites the copy's build.ninja to reference the ORIGINAL tree's absolute source paths
classification_rationale: a revert-check run that way silently recompiles the UNMUTATED tracked source while reporting results against the mutated file - a false-green in the verification method itself, which is precisely the channel this gate exists to close.
summary: Caught by noticing the object file would not rebuild after touch, and by diffing the copied build.ninja's literal source path. Fixed with a genuine fresh meson setup in the scratch tree. Recorded because it invalidates the obvious way to do revert-checks in this repo; the senior's own revert-check for rotation_warn_dedup avoided it only by compiling a standalone TU rather than copying a build dir.

trigger: describe() without a companion counter() leaves the family absent from /metrics
classification_rationale: re-verified at Gate 8 by standalone compile against sdk/include/yuzu/metrics.hpp: the pre-fix shape emits NOTHING, not even a # TYPE line; the fixed shape emits the series at 0. counter(name) reaches labels({}), which inserts a zero-valued Counter into the family's instances_ map, and that insertion is what serialize() enumerates.
summary: Not cosmetic - the reviewer specifically tested the possibility that a bare counter(name) might not emit a zero sample, which is the way this fix could have been hollow.

trigger: the senior renamed the never-shipped capped counter kind-neutral while its shipped sibling keeps the engine prefix, deciding it in sre's absence
classification_rationale: ENDORSED, not merely accepted. The reviewer established by git log -S plus merge-base --is-ancestor that ..._sweep_failures_total came in via be598ddf, an ancestor of this branch's merge-base with dev - so it is genuinely shipped and the do-not-rename justification is factually grounded rather than a rationalization.
adjudicated_by: sre governance agent, not the change author

Residual cost - a prefix scan misses the capped counter - is disclosed in both HELP strings and cross-referenced in both directions in metrics.md.

classification_rationale: bounded blast radius - only alert-on-absence fidelity, not count correctness - so SHOULD, not a floor.

trigger: the Gate 8 re-review brief told sre that SRE-F2, SRE-F3 and the gauge recommendation were all deferred to #2969; F3 was actually filed in #2970 section D
classification_rationale: the ISSUES are correct and correctly attributed - #2970's origin line names sre F3 explicitly. The brief was wrong, and the reviewer reasonably concluded from the brief plus #2969 alone that a finding had been dropped without disposition.

Same root cause each time: asserting a detail from memory or from a subagent's self-report rather than checking it. Cross-reference comment added to #2969 so a future auditor does not repeat the inference.

trigger: a future edit reverting the REST arm's "partial" audit outcome to "failure"
classification_rationale: re-verified at Gate 8 by the reporter that RAISED it, independently of the fix agent's self-report: fresh git worktree, genuine meson setup (never copying build-linux, the QE-METHOD trap it documented itself), full 455-target build, mutation applied in the scratch tree only, ninja confirmed to recompile and relink so the mutation was actually picked up.

The reporter also checked WHY it can observe what it asserts: rotate_token issues no further query referencing `name` after the hook fires, so the mint genuinely commits; the poisoned column is hit by list_active_for_principal on a DIFFERENT pooled connection, which is the branch under test; and ground truth is read on a third connection whose column list avoids the renamed column, so the test asserts against reality rather than against the branch it drove.

trigger: an SRE authoring a stuck-pair alert on increase(...{reason="successor_unused"}) to the documented cadence, or a maintainer restoring per-tick emission to match the design doc's normative text
classification_rationale: I4: both docs promise a loud repeating signal on the audit/metric channel for the zero-usable-credential state; an alert built to that spec fires once and never again, so the stuck pair is concealed on exactly the channels an operator alerts from. The design doc is the sharpest instance on this branch - it DEFINES the warning as 'an audit row plus a metric' and then says they are 'no longer deduplicated once elapsed'. auth-architecture.md is a ROUTED doc, i.e. the copy a future security-guardian loads.
summary: The same defect class the previous round claims to have closed, two layers out. Root cause is mine: my fix brief named the three sites CA-F2 listed instead of asking for a repo-wide sweep of the CLAIM. Fixed by sweeping the claim pattern across docs/, .claude/ and changelog.d/ - which found exactly these two and nothing else - and both corrected sites now state all three cadences explicitly and point at #2969 for the alertable signal.

trigger: a maintainer reading ApiTokenStore's PUBLIC contract for sweep_expired_rotations or list_rotations_nearing_expiry_unused, or the comment directly above the RotationWarnDedup object that falsifies it; or an alert author who greps the source rather than the user manual
classification_rationale: I4: the store header DEFINES the warning as an audit row plus a counter and then says they re-fire every tick 'so a stuck pair cannot go silent'.
